          "text": "# Alpha Hyi: A Southern Star on the Move\n\n*An easy naked-eye target in Hydrus, this F-type subgiant offers a quiet lesson in how stars shift across the sky.*\n\nIn the southern constellation Hydrus, Alpha Hyi is bright enough to see without optical aid\u2014and close enough to the celestial pole that it can be hard to reach from much of the Northern Hemisphere. Its light has crossed roughly 63 light-years to meet us. Yet the star\u2019s more surprising story is written not in its brightness but in its motion: Alpha Hyi is a high-proper-motion star, changing position against the more distant background of the sky.\n\nThe SIMBAD astronomical database lists Alpha Hyi as spectral type F0IV, with a visual magnitude of 2.84. The \u201cF0\u201d describes its spectral class; \u201cIV\u201d is the luminosity class for a subgiant. In other words, it is not classified as an ordinary main-sequence star, though the catalog entry alone doesn\u2019t tell us its precise age or future.
